role: Interpretation half of AnalysisSummaryGenerator: HRV band (personal vs age-adjusted), the 0-100 diagnostic score, headline title/icon, 'What This Means' explanation, probable causes, key findings and trend insight sentences; plus ExplanationCopy (per-band paragraph builders).
types: ExplanationCopy: enum — 'What This Means' paragraph builders per RMSSDCategory
ExplanationCopy.Inputs: struct — preformatted values the builders read
toplevel: DiagnosticPoints constants: base 50; RMSSD excellent 40/good 30/fair 20/reduced 10/low -10; stress low 20/normal 15/elevated 10/high 0/very high -15; LF/HF optimal 20/parasympathetic 15/moderate 5/sympathetic -10; DFA optimal 20; ANS balance +15/+10/-5/-15. Max raw total 165 and min -40 before clamping to 0...100.

flags.text: The comment on ansBalanceFindings says the narrative must not read autonomic-state verdicts off a single LF/HF value (Billman 2013), yet ExplanationCopy.fair says 'There's some sympathetic activation present' solely because lfhf > 2.0, and the +Steps copy says 'your nervous system is still activated' solely from lfhf > 3.0.

keyFindings and trendInsight produce the same judgements twice with near-identical copy: recentAverageFindings/rmssdAverageInsights, personalBaselineFindings/rmssdBaselineInsights, restingHRFindings/restingHRInsights, sevenDayTrendFindings/sevenDayTrendInsights.

Missing metrics are substituted with 'normal' values (stress 150, LF/HF 1.0, DFA 1.0) in the explanation and cause context, so a reading lacking ANS/frequency/DFA results can qualify as isGoodReading and have its negative causes suppressed.

units.does: Maps biologicalSex (.male/.female, else nil) to AgeAdjustedHRV.Sex and returns AgeAdjustedHRV.interpret for tonight's RMSSD, userAge and sex.
HRV band: personalCategory(ratio rmssd/canonicalBaselineRMSSD) when a positive canonical baseline exists, else the age-adjusted population category.

branches.effect: population ageAdjustedInterpretation.category; else personal ratio band

units.does: Bands a ratio to baseline: >=1.15 excellent, >=0.85 good, >=0.70 fair, >=0.60 reduced, else low.
Diagnostic score: 50 + RMSSD band points + stress-index points + LF/HF points + 20 if DFA α1 in [0.75,1.0] + ANS balance points, clamped to 0...100.

flags.text: Weights sum far above the range (max raw 165): a 'good' band (30) with normal stress (15) and in-range LF/HF (20) already clamps at 100, so the score cannot distinguish most decent nights; it becomes headlineScore whenever a session has no recovery score.

units.does: Points per RMSSD category: 40/30/20/10/-10.
ANS balance points from pns-sns: >=1.0 → +15, >=0 → +10, >=-1.0 → -5, else -15; 0 when either index missing.
Recovery score 0-100 for the headline: session.scoreBreakdown.compositeScore, else session.recoveryScore×10, else nil.

branches.effect: fall back to recoveryScore*10; nil if that is also nil

units.does: headline score: compositeHeadlineScore, else computeDiagnosticScore().

branches.effect: diagnostic score used instead (different scale semantics on the same ScoreVerdict ladder)

units.does: ScoreVerdict for headlineScore.
Headline title: verdict's English word when NarrativeLanguage.isEnglish, else its localized word.
Headline SF Symbol name from the verdict.
'What This Means' paragraph: dispatches on hrvCategory to the matching ExplanationCopy builder with explanationInputs.
Gathers formatted RMSSD, stress/LF-HF/DFA (with defaults), age note, sleep flags, awake minutes, formatted sleep and the sleep context sentence.

branches.effect: no canonical baseline → ' (<age phrase>)' or '' when no age; canonical baseline → '' (age note dropped)

units.does: Population age phrase for the age-adjusted category; nil when the interpretation has no ageContext (no age given).
One sleep sentence: short sleep, else fragmented, else low efficiency (<75%); nil when no sleep or none applies.

branches.effect: nil; else low-efficiency sentence with rounded percent

units.does: Good reading = isGoodRMSSD and stress < 200 and LF/HF < 2.5 and DFA < 1.2.
RMSSD good: >= 0.85×canonical baseline when one exists, else >= 40 ms absolute.

branches.effect: absolute rule rmssd >= 40; else ratio rule

units.does: Top-3 probable causes from CauseDetector over causeContext, converted to ProbableCause.

Builds CauseDetectionContext: metrics (stress/LF-HF/DFA defaulted), pNN50, isGoodReading, isExcellentReading (stats.hasData and rmssd > 1.15×avgRMSSD), tags, trend stats, sleep, sleep trend, session and earlier sessions.

flags.text: isExcellentReading is rmssd > 1.15×avgRMSSD alone; CauseDetector.detectCauses returns only positive causes when it is true (CauseDetector.swift:133), so a night with very high stress index or LF/HF but RMSSD 15% over average gets no negative causes.
Magic multiplier 1.15 for isExcellentReading inline instead of a named constant (the same idea uses 1.1 at line 436 and 0.95 at 243/435).

units.does: Key findings list: trend/baseline findings, age/band finding (given previous findings), stress, LF/HF, heart rhythm, window quality, beat variation, sleep, sleep trend (with isGoodHRV = rmssd >= 40 or rmssd >= 0.95×avg) and training load findings.

flags.text: isGoodHRV here uses the absolute 40 ms rule (or 0.95×avg), not the personal-baseline rule hrvCategory/isGoodRMSSD use, so a low-baseline user's normal night (e.g. 22 ms) is 'not good HRV' for the sleep-trend findings while the band calls it good.

units.does: Trend findings (needs stats): percent vs avgRMSSD sentence, personal 5-night baseline sentence, 7-day trend sentence and resting-HR sentence concatenated.
One sentence on RMSSD vs recent baseline by percent: >20 significantly higher, >10 above, <-20 significantly below, <-10 below, else none.

flags.text: For RMSSD >20% above the recent average this says 'excellent recovery today', and the steps (rmssdPct > 15) offer 'great day to push yourself'; TrendComparisonCard deliberately does not call such a jump excellent recovery because it can follow heavy training (parasympathetic saturation, Plews 2012). The summary and the card on the same night interpret the same jump in opposite ways.

units.does: Personal-baseline sentence (only without canonical baseline): >15% above or below the 5-night baseline.

branches.cond: canonical baseline present, or stats.baselineRMSSD nil/<=0

units.does: 7-day trend sentence: improving when trend7Day > 0, decline when < 0.

branches.effect: decline sentence; else [] (0 cannot occur since nil unless movement up/down)

units.does: Resting-HR sentence: meanHR more than 5 bpm above avgHR → elevated, more than 5 below → lower.

Band finding: when other findings exist, only 'This reading is <age phrase>' (population band, no canonical baseline) or nothing; when none, 'HRV is <band> at X ms' by hrvCategory with optional age suffix.

branches.effect: return age-phrase sentence or [] (when agePhrase nil); else band sentence

units.does: Stress index sentence: >300 high, >150 elevated, >50 normal, else low.
LF/HF sentence: >3.0 high (softened when pNN50 > 25 and RMSSD >= 40), <0.5 low, within [0.8,1.5] usual range, otherwise none.

branches.effect: 'common sleep-stage variation'; else 'above usual resting range — deep breathing…'
usual range sentence; else [] (0.5-0.8 and 1.5-3.0 silent)

units.does: DFA α1 sentence: >1.35 accumulated fatigue; >1.2 fatigue unless strong vagal tone; [0.75,1.0] in reference range; [0.60,0.75) less organized; else none.
Window-quality caveat when result.isOrganizedRecovery is false: DFA <0.65 'didn't settle', >1.15 'signs of fatigue', otherwise 'not fully consolidated'; no DFA → 'no deep recovery window'.

branches.effect: nil treated as organized → no caveat
DFA-specific sentences; else 'No deep recovery window' sentence

units.does: pNN50 sentence: <5 very low variation, >30 strong variation, else none.
Sleep findings (duration + efficiency) when sleep was recorded.
Sleep duration sentence: <300 min → remarkable (HRV > 1.1×avg) / solid (good HRV) / short-sleep-factor; >=420 min with HRV > 1.1×avg → great combo; else none.

branches.effect: solid sentence; else 'Short sleep… likely a major factor in reduced HRV'

flags.text: isGoodHRV is recomputed here with the identical expression already computed in keyFindings.

units.does: Sleep efficiency sentence: >=92% nearly uninterrupted; <75% with >360 min in bed → low efficiency with awake minutes; else none.
Sleep trend findings when sleep recorded and >=3 trend nights: direction sentence plus tonight-vs-average sentence (percent diff 0 when average is 0).

branches.cond: no sleep, no sleepTrend or nightsAnalyzed < 3

units.does: Direction sentence by trends.trend: declining always; improving only when isGoodHRV; stable only when avg >= 7 h and isGoodHRV; insufficient none.
Tonight-vs-average sentence when |diff| > 25%: above-average or below-average.

branches.effect: above sentence; else below sentence with average hours

flags.text: 25% threshold is an inline magic number (twice).

units.does: Training-load finding from the frozen trainingContext (or result.trainingContext): ACR <0.8 below usual, >1.5 jumped sharply, >1.3 above usual; without ACR, CTL and ATL both under ctlThreshold → very low activity.

branches.cond: trainingContext and result.trainingContext both nil ('??' + guard)
branches.effect: []; caller's context preferred over the result's

branches.cond: no ACR and ctl and atl < ctlThreshold

flags.text: Findings read only the frozen training context (caller's, else result's), while the push gate (+Steps adviceLoad) prefers liveLoadSnapshot; for today's session the summary can say 'Recent training is below your usual range' (frozen ACR) while the steps withhold the push for a live sharp increase. It also reads ACR without the ctl >= ctlThreshold qualification TrainingAdviceGate applies before trusting the ratio.

units.does: Trend paragraph: 'Record more sessions' without stats; else RMSSD-vs-average, baseline, resting HR, stress and 7-day trend insights joined, plus a 'trends will become more accurate' line when fewer than 7 sessions.

flags.text: trendInsight is consumed only by the assistant context (ContextBuilder.swift:212); the screen shows TrendComparisonCard.trendInsight, a near-copy with different copy for a >20% rise and different average fallbacks, so the assistant and the card can state different trend sentences for the same night.

units.does: RMSSD vs average insight: |pct| < 10 consistent; >20 significantly higher; >10 above; <-20 significantly below; <-10 below.

flags.text: For RMSSD >20% above the recent average this says 'excellent recovery today', and the steps (rmssdPct > 15) offer 'great day to push yourself'; TrendComparisonCard deliberately does not call such a jump excellent recovery because it can follow heavy training (parasympathetic saturation, Plews 2012). The summary and the card on the same night interpret the same jump in opposite ways.

units.does: Personal-baseline insight (only without canonical baseline): >15% below / above.

branches.cond: canonical baseline present or baselineRMSSD nil/<=0

units.does: Resting HR insight: >5 bpm above avg elevated; >5 below lower.
Stress insight when tonight's stress > 1.3×period average and > 200.

branches.cond: stress or avgStress nil, or stress <= 1.3×avg, or stress <= 200

units.does: 7-day trend insight: improving (>0) or decline (<0).
Mid-sentence population age phrase per category.
Low-band paragraph: opening; short sleep → short-sleep explanation only; else reason by stress > 300, LF/HF > 3.0, or generic suppressed-parasympathetic text, plus sleep context.

branches.effect: LF/HF reason; else generic suppressed-parasympathetic reason

units.does: Reduced-band paragraph: short sleep → sentence; fragmented → sentence; else reason by DFA > 1.2, stress > 200 or generic, plus sleep context.
Excellent-band paragraph: good sleep + not fragmented + consolidated → fully ready; short sleep → capacity caveat; not consolidated → not sustained; stress < 100 → well-balanced; else neutral.

branches.effect: 'nervous system is well-balanced'; else neutral beat-to-beat sentence

flags.text: When stress is missing the input is the 150 default, so the 'stress < 100' branch can never fire for a reading without ANS metrics; the explanation silently picks the neutral sentence.

units.does: Good-band paragraph: good unfragmented sleep → well-positioned; short sleep → better-sleep sentence; else 'autonomic nervous system is well-balanced'.

flags.text: The fallback sentence 'Your autonomic nervous system is well-balanced.' (and fair()'s 'reasonably balanced', excellent()'s 'confirm your nervous system is well-balanced') is the exact autonomic-state verdict the ansBalanceFindings comment says the narrative must not issue; here it is issued with no LF/HF reading at all, purely because sleep was neither good nor short.

units.does: Fair-band paragraph: short sleep → sentence; LF/HF > 2.0 → 'some sympathetic activation present' + sleep context; else 'reasonably balanced'.

branches.effect: sympathetic-activation sentence + sleepContext; else reasonably-balanced (no sleepContext)

units.does: Joins the non-nil sentences with a space.
